plugins.latest_readme:
# Discworld Blorpsack

A [Mallard](https://mallard.vnsf.xyz) plugin for [Discworld MUD](https://discworld.starturtle.net/lpc/) that tracks **blorps** — pieces of jewellery enchanted to remember a location — carried by your character, and broadcasts the list for other plugins (e.g. cowtography) to route to.

Blorpsack has no routing or mapping logic of its own. Its whole job is
registering blorps and telling other plugins where they are.

## Commands

Commands use Mallard's client command prefix — `/` by default. Blorps are
stored per character, so a fresh character starts with an empty list even
on the same account and world.

```
/blorp                  — list all registered blorps
/blorp add <name>       — register a blorp named <name> at your current room
/blorp rm <name>        — remove a blorp
```

Adding a blorp with a name that already exists overwrites its stored room
silently — that's how you re-register a blorp after recasting it
somewhere new.

```
/blorp add market        Registered blorp "market" at The Mended Drum.
/blorp                   Blorps:
                            market               The Mended Drum
/blorp rm market          Removed blorp "market".
```

## Panel

An optional "Blorpsack" panel shows the same list with Add/Remove
controls. It's a pure convenience layer over the commands above — nothing
in this plugin requires opening it.

## For plugin authors: subscribing to the blorp list

Blorpsack broadcasts over Mallard's cross-plugin `events` bus:

- `broaty.discworld-blorpsack.blorps` — emitted after every successful
  `add`/`rm`, and in response to the request event below. Payload:
  `{ blorps = { { room_id = "...", name = "..." }, ... } }`.
- `broaty.discworld-blorpsack.blorps.request` — emit this once after your
  own plugin's load (e.g. after a short delay, to give blorpsack a chance
  to load too) to get the current list regardless of which plugin loaded
  first. Blorpsack never broadcasts unprompted at load.

```lua
events.on("broaty.discworld-blorpsack.blorps", function(data)
  -- data.blorps is an array of { room_id, name }
end)

events.emit("broaty.discworld-blorpsack.blorps.request", {})
```

## Installation

Install from the Mallard marketplace.

## AI disclosure

Much of this plugin's code was written with the help of an LLM (Claude).
Design decisions, testing, and review are the author's own.

plugins.latest_readme:
# Bosse's Discworld Greg Tracker

Tracks each skeleton warrior raised with Grisald's Reanimated Guardian on
[Discworld MUD](https://discworld.starturtle.net/), from the moment it rises to the
moment you lose control of it, and builds lifetime statistics grouped by cause of
death and fierceness.

## Use

Raise a skeleton as usual. The tracker picks up the rise line and the "you mentally
take control" line automatically, then parses its fierceness the next time you look
at it. Nothing further is needed — just play, and check the **Greg** panel or type
`greg` for a status line.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `greg` | Uptime, fierceness, and how it compares to past runs |
| `greg stats` | Lifetime statistics |
| `greg list [n]` | The last n runs (default 10) |
| `greg died [cause]` | Close the current run by hand — `expired`, `slain`, `killed` or `unknown` |
| `greg fix <cause>` | Reclassify the most recent run |
| `greg debug` | Toggle parse echoing |
| `greg forget` | Discard the current run without recording it |
| `greg reset confirm` | Erase all recorded runs |

Both `greg …` and `/greg …` work. If the bare form gets in the way, turn off
**"Accept 'greg ...' typed without the command prefix"** in the plugin's settings.

## How death is classified

Only old-age deaths ("expired") describe how long a skeleton actually lives —
everything else was cut short for a reason the tracker already knows, and is counted
separately rather than averaged in:

- **Killed by you** — your own killing blow landed within the last 10 seconds.
- **Killed by something else** — control was lost with no recent kill and no recent
  old-age warning.
- **Died of old age** — the old-age warning ("*You feel your mental connection to the
  skeleton weakening…*") fired within the last 5 minutes. This is the only death that
  announces itself in advance, which is what makes the other two distinguishable at
  all.
- **Replaced by a new raise** — a new skeleton was raised while the tracker still
  thought the last one was alive (missed death line, disconnect, etc).

## The panel

The **Greg** panel is the current skeleton, in two lines: uptime and fierceness on
the first, and on the second how far through the expected lifetime it is alongside
its TPA (Transcendent Pneumatic Alleviator) shield state — up, or which colour it
has faded to on its way to breaking. Between them, once at least one skeleton has
died of old age, a progress bar against the expected lifetime for that fierceness
tier (falling back to the overall average until three runs of that tier exist).
Once the old-age warning fires the projection is pointless, so the bar goes and the
line reads **FAILING** with how long ago the warning landed.

A stripe down the left edge carries the state — the fierceness accent while a run is
healthy, amber once it is past its expected lifetime, red once it is failing, and
grey when nothing is up. It is what makes the panel findable in a stacked sidebar
without reading it. Figures that don't fit on a line aren't lost: the average behind
the percentage, and total uptime while failing, are on hover.

It deliberately fits in a few centimetres of panel height. The statistics and the
run history are `greg stats` and `greg list` — read once in a while, not worth
standing chrome.

## Notes

- **Runs are kept per character.** The same account raising on two characters won't
  average one skeleton's lifetime against the other's. Storage isn't touched until
  the character name actually arrives over GMCP (0.1.6+) — earlier versions could
  read (and then overwrite) the wrong bucket for an instant at boot, which looked
  like every recorded run had vanished after a Mallard restart or plugin reload.
- **The panel follows your Mallard theme** (0.1.2+), light, dark, or tinted — it
  previously always rendered in one fixed dark palette regardless of theme.
- **No permissions beyond `char.info`/`char.info.name`**, used only to key storage per character.
  The plugin never sends anything to the MUD and makes no network requests.
- **Timestamps come from `os.time()`**, so runs are timed whether or not the panel is
  open.
- **TPA tracking is derived entirely from the shield's own visible glow** (0.1.7+) —
  there's no command that reports it. The colour isn't a one-way ladder: it moves
  between dull red / bright red / wobbling orange / flickering yellow in either
  direction as the shield takes damage or recovers, drops back to no colour when
  fully healed, and clears to "Down" on the shield actually breaking (a different
  message entirely). The panel shows the same colour you'd see in the game window.
  If [discworld-magic](https://github.com/wizardquack/mallardx-discworld-magic) is
  also installed, its shield broadcast is used as a second, independent source for
  the same state (0.1.8+) — not a dependency, just a bonus: this plugin fully
  tracks TPA on its own either way.

## Requirements

Mallard 0.24.0 or later. No other plugins needed.

## Development

See [DEVELOPING.md](DEVELOPING.md) for building, sideloading and the port history.

## License

MIT

# Bosse's Discworld Vault Tracker

Remembers what is inside your vaults on [Discworld MUD](https://discworld.starturtle.net/),
one per room, and keeps a searchable list of everything you have stashed anywhere.

Look in a vault container once and Vault Tracker records its contents. From then on
you can browse, search and gauge the fullness of every vault from anywhere, across
sessions — without walking back.

## Use

Stand in the room containing a vault, then:

```
vault register <name>
```

Now just `look in <container>` — `l drawer`, say. The first look locks that vault to
that container and records everything in it.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `vault register <name>` | Register the room you are standing in |
| `vault list` | List registered vaults |
| `vault show [name]` | Print a vault's contents to the output window |
| `vault find <text>` | Search every vault for an item |
| `vault unlock [name]` | Re-bind a vault to a different container |
| `vault forget <name>` | Unregister a vault |

Both `vault …` and `/vault …` work. If the bare form gets in the way, turn off
**"Accept 'vault ...' typed without the command prefix"** in the plugin's settings.

## What changed since you last looked

Every look at a vault is compared against the one before it, and anything that moved
is reported under the list (0.2.2+):

```
[Vault Tracker] Updated vault 'AM vault' - 12 item entries.
[Vault Tracker] New since your last look: a bone amulet, three gold coins.
[Vault Tracker] Gone since your last look: a silver ring.
```

Quantities are ignored for this: `three gold coins` becoming `two gold coins` — or
`a gold coin` — is the same item, not a departure and an arrival. The first look at a
vault reports nothing, having nothing to compare against.

Walking into a registered vault room whose record has gone stale prints one line:

```
[Vault Tracker] You're in 'AM vault'. Last recorded 34 days ago - look in the drawer to refresh it.
```

The threshold is **"Remind me when a vault's record is this many days old"** in the
plugin's settings, 14 days by default. Set it to 0 to turn the reminder off.

## The panel

The **Vaults** panel gives one tab per vault, each with a fullness dot running from
green (empty) through to red (completely full), and "almost completely full" called
out separately in orange-red — that being the one worth acting on before your next
delivery bounces.

Contents are sorted alphabetically ignoring the leading quantity word, so "a black
backpack" files under B rather than under A with everything else. The search box at
the top searches every vault at once as you type; click a `[vault name]` on a hit to
jump straight to that vault's tab.

## Notes

- **One container per room.** Each vault is keyed to its room's GMCP identifier, and
  the first container you look in there claims it. Looking in your backpack afterwards
  won't overwrite the record. Use `vault unlock` if it bound to the wrong one.
- **Nothing here is specific to the guild vaults.** Any room that reports a GMCP
  identifier and any container that lists its contents when looked in will work —
  a chest in a rented player home, for instance.
- **Contents are only as current as your last look.** The timestamp above each list
  tells you how stale a record is, and walking back into the room reminds you when
  that record has gone stale (0.2.2+). Timestamps come from `os.time()` since 0.2.2;
  before that a vault recorded while the panel was shut carried no date at all and
  showed an em dash forever.
- **Vaults are kept per character** (0.2.0+). Two characters on the same Mallard
  install used to share one list; upgrading carries your existing vaults forward
  automatically. Storage isn't touched until the character name actually arrives
  over GMCP (0.2.1+) — earlier versions could read (and then overwrite) the wrong
  bucket for an instant at boot, which looked like every vault had vanished after
  a Mallard restart or plugin reload.
- **The panel follows your Mallard theme** (0.2.0+), light, dark, or tinted — it
  previously always rendered in one fixed dark palette regardless of theme.
- **No permissions beyond `room.info` and `char.info`/`char.info.name`** (the
  latter two only to key storage per character). The plugin never sends anything
  to the MUD and makes no network requests.

## Requirements

Mallard 0.24.0 or later. No other plugins needed.

## Development

See [DEVELOPING.md](DEVELOPING.md) for building, sideloading and the port history.

## License

MIT

plugins.latest_readme:
# Bosse's Discworld XP Goals

Pick an XP total to aim for on [Discworld MUD](https://discworld.starturtle.net/) —
the price of a guild title, the next batch of levels, whatever you are saving towards
— and a small panel keeps the gap in front of you: the goal, your current XP, what is
left, and how far along you are.

It redraws the moment a new XP figure arrives rather than on a timer, reads your XP
three different ways so it works with or without MXP, and keeps a separate goal for
every character on the account.

## Use

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `xpg <amount>` | Set a goal (commas ok, e.g. `xpg 5,000,000`) |
| `xpg clear` | Clear the current goal |
| `xpg` | Show the current goal and how much is left |
| `xpg help` | List the above in the output window |

Both `xpg …` and `/xpg …` work. Amounts may be written with or without commas.

## The panel

Open **XP Goal** from the panel list:

```
Goal      5,696,459 xp
Current   3,125,000 xp
2,571,459 xp left
[███████████░░░░░░░░░░░]  54% there
```

Before the first XP figure arrives the panel says so rather than guessing at one,
and once you pass the goal the line becomes **Goal reached!**

## Settings

In Mallard's plugin manager, under this plugin:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accept `xpg ...` typed without the command prefix | **on** | Lets you type `xpg` bare as well as `/xpg`. Turn it off if something else wants the word. |
| Set the goal automatically from `teachers cost` replies | **off** | See below. |

## Setting a goal from a teacher's price

Off by default — tick **"Set the goal automatically from 'teachers cost' replies"**
in the plugin's settings to turn it on. Then pricing something up sets the goal for
you. Ask the MUD what it costs —

```
teachers cost 10 fi.de.do
```

— and the reply *"To learn 10 levels of fighting.defence.dodging from an optimal
teacher would cost you 5696459."* becomes the goal, announced in the output so it is
never a silent change. The quoted price **is** the goal rather than something added
to your current XP, because that XP is spent out of the same total the panel tracks.

It replaces whatever goal was set before, which is why it is off until you ask for
it. Only that checkbox controls it — Mallard's Lua API can read plugin settings but
not write them, so there is no command that flips it.

## How current XP is read

No command reports XP on demand, so this reads it the same way
[discworld-vitals](https://github.com/wizardquack/mallardx-discworld-vitals) does,
without depending on that plugin being installed:

1. **MXP entity push** — the primary real-time path.
2. **GMCP `char.vitals`** — authoritative on login, and on some configs a periodic
   refresh too.
3. **The classic score-brief text line** (`Hp: … Gp: … Xp: … Burden: …%`), as a
   fallback for anyone with MXP disabled — only trusted when a `Burden` field is
   present, since burden-less variants of that line are combat-monitor spam rather
   than a real vitals line.

## Notes

- **Goals are kept per character.** The same account raising XP on two characters
  won't mix their goals up. Storage isn't touched until the character name actually
  arrives over GMCP, avoiding the boot-race bug found in earlier ports of Vault
  Tracker / Greg Tracker (an empty name for an instant at boot could otherwise
  overwrite a real character's saved goal).
- **The panel follows your Mallard theme** — light, dark, or tinted.
- **No permissions beyond `char.vitals`/`char.info`**, used only to read XP and key
  storage per character. The plugin never sends anything to the MUD.

## Requirements

Mallard 0.24.0 or later. No other plugins needed.

## Development

- `dev-install.ps1` links this working copy into Mallard's `plugins-dev` folder via
  a junction (no admin rights needed) — an edit is live after "Reload plugins" and a
  reconnect (the Lua VM is only created at world connect).
- `build.ps1` assembles the `.mallardx` archive for distribution.

## License

MIT

# Being's Discworld Alias Helper

A Mallard plugin for recording, searching and managing your Discworld MUD aliases. The panel uses the same compact, theme-aware styling as Being's Discworld Blorp Recorder. Requires Mallard 0.28.0 or later.

## Install

Download [version 1.1.0](https://github.com/bytechipper/beings-discworld-alias-helper/releases/download/v1.1.0/beings-discworld-alias-helper-1.1.0.mallardx), then install it with **Plugin manager → Install from file…**. Enable it for your Discworld world and open **Being's Discworld Alias Helper** from the panels menu. Allow sends and character GMCP access when requested.

![Alias list with category labels, searches and category filter](docs/panel-preview.png)

![Alias editor with category and content fields](docs/editor-preview.png)

## Use

1. Log in and wait for the panel to show your character's name. Discworld GMCP must be enabled.
2. Press **Start record**, then type `alias` in the MUD. The button starts listening; it does not type the command for you.
3. Let the whole list finish, including all pages if the MUD paginates it, then press **Stop record**. While recording, avoid unrelated commands or conversations that look like `name: content`.
4. Use **Search alias names** to filter names, **Search alias content** to filter commands inside aliases, and the **Category** dropdown to select a recorded category or **All categories**. All active filters must match. Searches ignore case and match literal text; each has its own **Clear** button. Categories are shown beside every alias, and the dropdown shows their saved alias counts.
5. Click an alias to open its editable content and **Category** field. Choose a recorded category from the suggestions or type a new name, then press **Save to MUD**. Use `default` to move an alias out of a named category. **Delete alias** asks for confirmation before sending `unalias <name>`.
6. Use **Add new alias** for an empty dialog with a name field and content area. Its category starts with the selected filter, or `default` when viewing all categories, and can be changed before saving. To overwrite a recorded name, open it from the list instead.

Alias bodies must be one logical line: use semicolons between MUD commands. The text area wraps long lines visually. `$*$`, `$1$`, `$arg:default$`, backslashes and punctuation are preserved. Existing names are read-only; changing an alias's name is outside this plugin's scope.

The recorder recognises both `name: content` and `name (colour replace): content`. The `(colour replace)` annotation is a listing label, so it is excluded from the saved name and content. After updating from 1.0.2 or earlier, record `alias` again to add previously skipped entries; clearing the saved list first is optional.

Content edits send `alias <name> <content>`, or `alias <name> in "<category>" <content>` to preserve a non-default category. Category-only edits send `alias set category <name> <category>` without rewriting content. If both fields change, the content command is sent first, followed by the category command. New aliases can be created directly in a chosen category. Category names cannot contain quotes, backslashes, semicolons or control characters. The MUD receives commands directly, bypassing client aliases and input processing. Reserved command names and bulk deletion forms are rejected.

Record `alias` once to populate categories, or record `alias show category sailing` to update only that category. Existing saved categories appear automatically after upgrading. The category dropdown is based on recorded aliases; category summaries from `alias show categories` are ignored so their counts never become bogus aliases. The dropdown returns to **All categories** when switching characters or when its selected category disappears from the saved list.

The list updates locally after sending a command. **Check MUD output for confirmation**: the plugin does not infer success from arbitrary server responses. After an error, record `alias` again to refresh. Recording merges entries and updates changed content; it does not remove entries absent from a listing, because the listing may be partial. Deletes made through this panel remove the saved entry. Prefer the panel's delete action for recorded aliases, since deletions made elsewhere leave a stale saved entry.

Lists persist separately for each character and world. Switching characters or disconnecting stops recording and closes any open editor. A stale editor cannot overwrite an alias changed by a fresh recording. Recording never sends a command.

Use `/aliases_clear` to clear all saved aliases for the current character in this world and stop recording. This clears the plugin's stored list only; it sends no commands to the MUD and keeps other characters' lists. Then start recording and type `alias` to build a fresh list. If you use a custom Mallard command prefix, use it instead of `/`.

## Development

Built against [Mallard's v0.28.0 plugin development guide](https://mallard.vnsf.xyz/docs/mallard-plugin-dev-v0.28.0.html) and [API reference](https://mallard.vnsf.xyz/docs/api-reference-v0.28.0.html). No external services or panel libraries are required.

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v  # Python 3.11+ and liblua5.4
python3 tests/panel_test.py             # Playwright with Chromium installed
python3 scripts/build.py               # Reproducible .mallardx archive
```

The runtime tests use invented examples and a generated 1530-alias listing, including 19 `(colour replace)` entries. They exercise category creation and moves, command validation and character changes, and check persistence and failure handling. Browser tests cover visible categories, combined filters and category editing using a mocked Mallard bridge. Player exports stay local and are ignored by Git. A live Discworld session is still needed to confirm server acceptance of commands.

For unpacked development, use a directory named `net.discworld.beings-discworld-alias-helper` in Mallard's dev plugins folder, then reload plugins.

# Being's Discworld Armour Helper

An offline Mallard plugin styled like Being's Discworld Spell Library. Includes all 270 entries in the supplied wiki's Armours table, searchable by name, material, body part and clothing layer. Select an item to open its statistics, documented infobox facts, full article, and wiki source in a keyboard-accessible dialog. Custom Ug Ogg entries without individual articles retain the index's descriptions and statistics.

Install the `.mallardx` archive through Mallard's plugin manager. Connect to Discworld and type **coverage** in the normal MUD input. The plugin observes that exact command without overriding it or sending any commands. Recommendations appear in the Armour Helper panel. Repeat coverage after changing equipment. Data is cleared on disconnect and is never stored or sent elsewhere.

Choose balanced, sharp, pierce, blunt, or protection per pound. The advisor identifies documented armour from the output, tracks layer capacity (including multi-layer items), and greedily chooses additions that improve the best documented rating on body parts. It also offers same-layer replacements that preserve coverage. Additions form one proposed set; replacements are independent alternatives to currently worn pieces. This is an estimate, not a proof of optimal combat performance: enchantment, item condition, fitting, shields, strength, race, attack frequency, and interactions between stacked layers are not inferred. Unknown clothing is shown explicitly because its layer usage and protection cannot be established. Omitted body parts are not treated as confirmed bare. `coverage on ...`, `coverage of ...`, and `coverage unprotected` do not replace the equipment snapshot.

## Build and verify

```
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The generated catalogue is bundled; no runtime network or Python dependencies are required. To refresh it from a backup, install `beautifulsoup4` and run:

```
python3 scripts/import_wiki.py /path/to/wiki
```

Code is MIT licensed. Wiki content remains under its original terms; see NOTICE and the source links.

# Being's Discworld Blorp Recorder

A Mallard plugin listing saved blorp identifications in a dockable panel, styled like Being's Discworld XP Timers. Requires Mallard 0.25.0 or later.

## Install

Install `dist/beings-discworld-blorp-recorder-1.0.4.mallardx` using **Plugin manager → Install from file…**, then enable it for your Discworld world. For development, place the unpacked plugin in Mallard's dev plugins folder and reload plugins.

## Panel preview

![Panel preview with sample blorps](docs/panel-preview.png)

This preview uses sample data in a standalone browser.

## Commands

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `/blorps_rec_start` | Start recording identifications in incoming MUD text. |
| `/blorps_rec_stop` | Stop recording. |
| `/blorps` | Print all saved places and recording status. |
| `/blorps_remove dojo` | Remove the exact identification `dojo`. |
| `/blorps_remove two words` | Remove an identification containing spaces; do not add quotes. |

The panel has equivalent Start Recording, Stop Recording, and per-place Go and See buttons and small red trash icons. Go sends `go <identification>` and See sends `see <identification>` directly to the MUD; the plugin requires send permission. Recording starts off on plugin load and stops on disconnect. Starting again adds to the existing list.

The search bar at the top instantly filters places by case-insensitive substring. Clear or manually emptying the field shows all places again. The search stays active when the list updates; the count shows matches / total while filtering. Recording controls occupy a compact strip.

After starting recording, run your usual `locate necklaces in pack`, look, inventory, or other commands. Every nonempty string between `("` and `")` in an incoming line is captured, regardless of item type. Multiple identifications on a single line are supported. The list is sorted and deduplicated by the exact, case-sensitive identification, so two items identified as `dojo` produce one place. Removing a place allows it to be recorded again if seen while recording is active. No item-type filter is applied, so any incoming text with that syntax can be captured during recording.

## Persistence

Each addition and removal is saved immediately through Mallard's persistent JSON `storage` API, under key `blorps`, separately for each world and plugin. The saved value has the form `{ "version": 1, "places": ["casino", "dojo"] }`. Failed writes are reported and leave the saved and displayed list unchanged.

Mallard's Lua sandbox removes `io` and `os` and documents `storage` as its persistence mechanism. This plugin therefore uses host-managed JSON storage rather than writing a user-selected text file. The UI does not claim a successful save when storage raises an error.

API reference used: [Mallard plugin development guide v0.25.0](https://mallard.vnsf.xyz/docs/mallard-plugin-dev-v0.25.0.html), especially persistent storage, world events, custom panels, theming, and local development.

## Verification

Run `rpmlua tests/recorder_test.lua` (Lua 5.3) from the plugin directory. The test exercises the entry point against mocked Mallard APIs, including the supplied examples, recording boundaries, unrestricted item types, multiple identifications, duplicate suppression, removal, reload persistence, panel messages, disconnect, invalid stored data, and storage write failures. Browser panel checks passed with a mocked Mallard bridge. Run `python3 tests/panel_test.py` in an environment with Playwright and Chromium installed to repeat the search, clear, recording status, button spacing, and Go/See/remove checks. An actual Mallard client smoke test is still needed for host integration.

## Build

Run `python3 scripts/build.py` with Python 3.11 or later. The build includes only the manifest, Lua source, panel assets, license, and README, with fixed ZIP timestamps for repeatable output. For marketplace CI, run `python3 scripts/build.py net.discworld.beings-discworld-blorp-recorder.mallardx`.

## Compatibility and testing

Validated against Mallard 0.27.0 (API 1.0). Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` with the Lua 5.4 shared library installed. Run `python3 tests/panel_test.py` with Playwright and Chromium installed. Build with `python3 scripts/build.py`.

# Being's Discworld Kill Counter

An offline reference for 116 current Discworld spells, styled like Being's Discworld Blorp Recorder. Requires Mallard 0.27.0 or later.

## Using the library

Expand a spell book to read its locations and details. Close with × or Escape.

The library contains all current entries in the supplied wiki's wizard and witch spell tables. Retired/lost spells are excluded. Data reflects that backup, not live game updates. Missing information is identified rather than invented. Green-chart bonus suggestions are approximate readings of the wiki charts and do not guarantee success; learning levels and written recommendations remain in the spell article.

plugins.latest_readme:
# Discworld Autocols

Automatically toggles the server-side `cols` setting around column-aware commands.

## What it does

Mallard encourages users to set `cols` to 999 columns to minimize
problems with server-side word-wrap interfering with trigger matching.
However, many Discworld commands like `inv`, `who`, `help`, and
`skills` respond with decorative banners padded to your advertised
width — which becomes 999-character visual noise when displayed in a
reasonably-sized window.

This plugin intercepts those commands, temporarily sets `cols` to your live
OutputPane width (read via `mud.viewport()`), sends the command, and restores
`cols` to 999 afterwards. The result is readably-formatted command output sized
to your actual pane — wider pane, wider banners — while preserving trigger-safe
server-side wrapping for normal prose.

## Wrapped commands

The plugin automatically wraps the following commands:

- **Single-shot** (toggle narrower, send, toggle back): `alias`, `blog`, `cost`,
  `countries`, `group status`, `help`, `inv` / `inventory`, `lang` / `language`,
  `nickname`, `quest`, `rituals`, `skills`, `sp` / `speak`, `spells`, `syntax`,
  `who`
- **Stateful modes** (stay narrow until explicit exit): `mail`, `title quest`

## Column width

The narrow width follows your OutputPane: drag the pane wider and banners get
wider; drag it narrower and they shrink. The `mail` and `title quest` modes
also re-send `cols N` when you resize mid-session so subsequent prompts match.

## Adding your own commands

The plugin exposes an **Extra commands to wrap** setting (per world, so each
character can have its own list). Add any command word that produces banner
output you'd like sized to your pane.

- Separate entries with commas: `skp, taa, score`
- An entry may contain spaces for multi-word commands: `look mailbox, read runes`
- Use a pipe to list synonyms for one entry: `skp|skillpoints`
- Only letters, digits, spaces, `_`, `-`, and `|` are allowed inside an entry
- If you re-declare a command that's already wrapped (e.g. `skills`), your entry
  is ignored with a warning

## Known limitation: abbreviations

Aliases match exact command spellings. If you type `i` for `inventory` or
`w` for `who`, the plugin will not intercept them. Type the full command name
(`inventory` or `who`) for the plugin to engage.

## Credit

Many thanks to Oki and their scripts at
https://code.tubul.net/tt_dw/scripts for the clever idea and
inspiration for this plugin.

plugins.latest_readme:
# Discworld Cowtography

A [Mallard](https://mallard.vnsf.xyz) plugin for [Discworld MUD](https://discworld.starturtle.net/lpc/) combining a minimap panel with a searchable database of rooms, shop items, NPC items and NPCs — with GMCP-driven speedwalk to any result.

Map data from **[Quow's Cow Bar and Minimap](https://quow.co.uk/minimap.php)**.

---

## Map panel

The map panel opens automatically on the right side of the window. As you walk through the MUD it tracks your position and highlights it on the map. Zoom in and out with the `+` and `−` buttons. Hover over the map to see room names.

**Keyboard navigation:** Click the map or press `Ctrl+Shift+m` to focus it, then use arrow keys to pan and `+`/`−` to zoom. Press `Escape` to release focus and return keyboard input to the MUD.

**Click any room to route there.** The path is highlighted on the map and a footer appears at the bottom of the panel showing the destination and move count. Click **walk** to start walking, or **✕** to cancel. If a clicked room has no reachable route, a brief error message appears in the footer instead. Click **⌂** at any time to switch back to your current character map and centre on your position. Middle-mouse drag pans the map; left-drag on empty space also pans.

**World map:** When you travel between cities or through the Disc's terrain the panel automatically switches to a world map showing your position on the full Discworld. Road and river networks, terrain types and major location markers are all shown.

**Right-click the map** to open a context menu. On SVG city maps, a **Filters** section lets you toggle street name labels and staircase exits. The **Maps** section lists all available maps grouped by region — hover a region to see its maps and click one to jump to it. Click-to-route works normally on any map you browse to.

## ASCII Map panel

A second, independent panel shows Discworld's own live ASCII minimap —
the same colour grid the MUD can print above `look`/`glance` — fed
directly from the `room.map` GMCP frame. It updates automatically as you
move, with no per-room map data to author. Some locations (indoors,
special zones) have no map to show; the panel says so rather than
showing a stale grid.

**Zoom:** Scroll anywhere in the panel to zoom in and out. The zoom
level is remembered per character.

**Right-click the panel** for two commands that control whether
Discworld also prints the map inline above `look`/`glance` in your main
window (via `options output map`, all four contexts: `look`,
`lookcity`, `glance`, `glancecity`):

- **Show map in output** — sets them all to `top`.
- **Hide map in output** — sets them all to `off`, so the map only
  appears in this panel.

This panel is read-only otherwise in this version: no click-to-route.
Show or hide the panel itself like any other Mallard panel.

---

## Commands

Commands use Mallard's client command prefix — `/` by default, configurable in Mallard's settings. Type `/db` on its own to print a command reference in the MUD window.

### Searching

```
/db <room name>           — search rooms by name
/db npc <name>            — search NPCs by name
/db npc {<area>} <name>   — search NPCs filtered by area name
/db item <name>           — search items for sale in shops
/db npcitem <name>        — search items carried or sold by NPCs
```

Search is case-insensitive. Up to 10 reachable results are shown, sorted by distance from your current room.

```
/db drum
/db npc wizard
/db npc {AM} pawn
/db item long sword
/db npcitem dagger
```

### Routing and walking

After a search, pick a result by number to route there and start walking immediately:

```
/db drum
  DB Search: room — "drum"  (3 results, nearest first)
   1.  The Drum  ...
   2.  ...
/db 1
  Walking to "The Drum" — 12 moves.
```

```
/go         — start or resume walking the current route
/go clear   — cancel the current route
```

`/go` walks whatever route is currently set, whether it came from a `/db` search result or a `/bm` bookmark.

You can also click any room on the map to set a route directly, without running a search first.

> You must be in a room tracked by the map data for routing and distance sorting to work.

### Bookmarks

Save your current room as a named bookmark and route back to it at any time. Bookmarks are stored per character.

```
/bm                     — list all bookmarks
/bm add <name>          — bookmark current room as <name>
/bm rm <name>           — remove bookmark <name>
/bm <name>              — highlight route to <name>, then /go to go
```

```
/bm add market           — saves current room as "market"
/bm market               — routes to your "market" bookmark
/go                      — starts walking the highlighted route
```

Saving a bookmark with a name that already exists overwrites silently.

---

## Settings

Settings are in the Mallard plugin settings panel.

**Map style** — Switch between *SVG (vector)* maps and *PNG (classic pixel art)* maps. SVG maps are sharp at any zoom and show room types, exits, and route highlighting. PNG maps use the original pixel-art images from Quow's Cow Bar.

**Vector map theme** — *Follow Mallard* (default) or any of Mallard's bundled themes (Catppuccin, Dracula, Nord, Solarized, Tufte, …). Colours the SVG map with that theme regardless of Mallard's own theme — e.g. a white map in an otherwise dark client. Only the map itself changes; the panel header and footer keep following Mallard. Has no effect on PNG maps. The list is a snapshot of Mallard's bundled themes (refresh with `npm run build:themes`); custom themes from your own themes folder aren't listed.

**Walk arrival sound** — Optional chime to play when a `/go` completes.

**Brief/verbose look around walks** — When enabled, sends `brief look` before and `verbose look` after the movement commands of a route, so long walks don't flood the screen with full room descriptions.

**Blorp routing** — When enabled, and the Discworld Blorpsack plugin is installed with blorps registered, route results and search results show a tip when teleporting to a blorp would shorten (or enable) the route. Off by default.

**Minimum blorp savings** — How many moves a blorp teleport must save before cowtography suggests it, in both the route tip and search results. Default 5.

---

## Installation

Install from the Mallard marketplace.

---

## Updating the database

The map and search data are built from [Quow's Cow Bar and Minimap](https://quow.co.uk/minimap.php). When Quow releases an update, regenerate all data files:

```bash
npm install
npm run build:data
git add data/ src/data/ ui/data/ ui/maps/
git commit -m "chore: regenerate data from updated Quow DB"
```

This downloads `quow_cowbar.zip` directly from quow.co.uk, extracts the database and map images, and regenerates everything.

If you already have a local copy of the zip or the SQLite database:

```bash
npm run build:data -- --zip /path/to/quow_cowbar.zip
npm run build:data -- --db /path/to/_quowmap_database.db   # seed db only; no maps.lua, JS, or PNGs
```

---

## For plugin authors: routing API

Other Mallard plugins can ask Cowtography to route the player through one
or more rooms over the cross-plugin `events` bus. Cowtography never moves
the character on its own: walkable routes still need the player to type
`/go` (or click Walk), and requests are refused while a walk is in progress.

### Request a route

```lua
events.emit("cowtography:route", {
  request  = 1,                       -- optional, any value; echoed in the reply
  source   = "myplugin",              -- optional string identifying your plugin
  rooms    = { "room-id-1", "room-id-2" }, -- required: 1–500 room id strings
  label    = "Farming run",           -- optional; shown in the map panel
  walkable = false,                   -- optional, default true
})
```

- Room ids are Quow-database room ids (the same ids Cowtography shows and
  Blorpsack broadcasts), as plain strings.
- Stops are visited nearest-first from the player's current room. A stop
  the route passes through counts as visited. Duplicates and the current
  room are ignored. The route ends at the last stop; there is no return leg.
- `walkable = false` makes a display-only guide route: drawn in green,
  with no Walk button, and `/go` won't walk it.
- Without `label` (or with an empty one), the panel shows
  `Route from <source>` (or `Route`).
- `source`, if given, must be a non-empty string.

### Clear your route

```lua
events.emit("cowtography:route_clear", { request = 2, source = "myplugin" })
```

This only clears a route set through this API with the same `source`
(no `source` matches no `source`). It never clears a route the player
set with `/db`, `/bm` or a map click, and it is refused while the player
is walking your route.

### Replies

Every request and clear gets exactly one reply:

```lua
events.on("cowtography:route_result", function(r)
  -- route set: { request, source, ok = true, stops = n, moves = n, skipped = { ids } }
  -- clear:     { request, source, ok = true, cleared = true | false }
  -- error:     { request, source, ok = false, error = code, message = text }
end)
```

| `error` | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `invalid_payload` | Malformed payload (for example `rooms` missing, empty, over 500, or not all strings) |
| `location_unknown` | Cowtography doesn't know where the player is yet |
| `walk_in_progress` | The player is walking a route |
| `no_reachable_stops` | None of the rooms can be reached from the current room |
| `internal_error` | Unexpected error inside Cowtography; `message` has details |

`skipped` lists unknown or unreachable room ids. On errors Cowtography
prints nothing; showing the `message` to the player is up to you.

### Precedence

- Your route replaces whatever route is showing, unless a walk is in
  progress.
- Any route the player sets replaces yours, and a later clear from you
  replies `cleared = false`.
- A walkable route that hasn't been started is cleared when the player moves
  by hand (same as for routes the player sets), and your ownership goes with
  it. Use `walkable = false` for an overlay that should stay up while the
  player moves.
- If there's no reply at all, Cowtography isn't installed or hasn't loaded
  yet. Its handlers register at plugin load, so retry after a short delay.

---

## Credits

Map data, database content and pathfinding algorithm adapted from **[Quow's Cow Bar and Minimap](https://quow.co.uk/minimap.php)** plugin for MUSHClient by Quow. Used with gratitude.

---

## AI disclosure

Much of this plugin's code was written with the help of an LLM (Claude). Design decisions, testing, and review are the author's own.

# Discworld Grouping

Shows the active group's roster (group name + member list) with
per-member HP/GP bars in a compact panel.

## What it does

- Auto-tracks group join/leave events (yours and others').
- Per-member HP/GP bars update from the `gs` (group status brief)
  output. The user is in control — there's no background polling; the
  panel's `⟳` button (or typing `gs` yourself) refreshes everyone in
  one round-trip.
- Dead members are flagged with a `ghost` badge.
- The group leader is flagged with a gold `L` badge, read from the
  leader marker in `group status` output (`(L)` in brief form, the
  "current leader of the group" line in verbose form). The badge also
  moves the moment the game posts a `... is now the leader of the group.`
  line — no refresh needed.
- Empty placeholder when you're not in a group.
- A five-pill shield row (T C E B M) per member: TPA / CCC / EFF / BUG /
  MS. v1 wires TPA and EFF — including a per-player TPA glow ladder
  fed from passive combat output. CCC/BUG/MS are placeholders pending a
  follow-up. State flows from `discworld-magic` via the cross-plugin
  `net.mallard.discworld.shield.up/.down` event surface.

# Cross-plugin communication

This plugin has an optional dependency on the discworld-magic plugin.
If you have it, you will get richer information on shielding for each
group member.

## Development

```sh
luarocks install busted  # one-time
busted                   # run unit tests
```

The pure-Lua modules (`group`, `shield_store`, `status_maps`) are unit-
tested under `spec/`. `group.lua` is the roster state machine — its spec
covers membership, vitals, ghosting, and leader tracking.

## Credit

Many thanks to Quow, whose work on similar plugins was invaluable in
designing and building this one.

plugins.latest_readme:
# Discworld Magic

Colour highlights and inline annotations for Discworld magic spell output
(enchantment levels, Klein-bottle energy, Earhammer / PfG damage,
Delude shadow depth, and other people's offensive casts).

Also tracks magic states/events and emits relevant events for other
interested plugins to consume. Two initial consumers are the
discworld-grouping plugin, and the discworld-vitals plugin, both of
which can display richer magical shielding info if you also have this
plugin installed and active.

## `/spell` — spell info lookup

A `/spell` slash command for the ~115 Discworld spells.

```
/spell              list every spell, grouped by type, in columns
/spell <nick>       full info card — e.g. /spell wgs
/spell <skill>      every spell that checks that skill — e.g. /spell fire
/spell <fragment>   fuzzy match across nick / name / description
/spell help         usage banner
```

The full card shows name, type, GP, casting size, components, tome,
and the per-stage spellcheck table — each threshold cell colour-coded
so you can see at a glance which bonus tier you'd land in. Nicks in
list views are clickable; they drill straight into the full card.

With [discworld-vitals](https://github.com/wizardquack/mallardx-discworld-vitals)
installed and a snapshot captured (run its `/skills-refresh`), the
spellcheck table gains four extra columns per stage: success chance,
your current level + bonus in the stage's skill, and a hint at the
bonus delta needed to reach the next chance tier.

## `/spellskill` — spells by skill

The inverse lookup. `/spell wgs` asks *what skills does this spell check?*;
`/spellskill fire` asks *what spells check fire, and how close am I to each?*

```
/spellskill <skill>       spells checking that skill, likeliest cast first
/spellskill <skill> tm    same rows, ordered by TM likelihood
/spellskill help          usage banner + the list of skills spells check
```

Aliased to `/ss`. `/spell <skill>` reaches the default view too — the
dedicated command is how you get the `tm` ordering.

```
Spells using fire (16 spells, 17 stages)
  Bonus: 150   Level: 128   Ordered by: success chance
  nick   Spell                             Stage  Chance  Max   Need  Consumes
  fnp    Fyodor's Nimbus of Porterage        2/6     90%  160   +10b  -
  kof    Kamikaze Oryctolagus Flammula       2/4     90%  160   +10b  yes
  kof    Kamikaze Oryctolagus Flammula       4/4     90%  160   +10b  yes
  ...
```

- **One row per stage, not per spell.** A spell can check the same skill
  at two different stages with different thresholds (`kof` above), and the
  stage is what you're actually graded on. `Stage` reads *this stage / the
  spell's total*.
- **`Chance`** is the same math as the `/spell` card's spellcheck table —
  how many of the stage's ten thresholds your bonus clears. **`Max`** is
  the bonus for `>99%`, and **`Need`** the delta to it.
- **`Consumes`** flags whether casting costs you a component. Spells
  needing a *reusable* prop (a staff, a mirror) read `-` alongside those
  needing nothing at all — the column asks what a cast costs, not what it
  requires.
- Your bonus is constant down the listing (it's one skill), so it sits in
  the header rather than repeating in a column.
- Nicks are clickable and drill into the full `/spell` card.

`tm` ordering ranks by `p × (1−p)`, so the stages nearest a coin-flip —
where a teaching moment is likeliest — float to the top. Without a
`/skills-refresh` snapshot both modes drop the chance columns and fall
back to a max-bonus ladder, cheapest to master first.

## `/mindspace` — spell-memory budget

Wizards and witches can only hold so many spells in their head at once:
each spell has a *size* (its Mindspace cost), and the sum of your known
spells' sizes may not exceed your available mindspace — which is your
`magic.spells.special` bonus + 30.

This plugin tracks both halves and annotates the `spells` command:

- **Per-spell sizes.** In the `spells` listing, each spell name is tagged
  with its mindspace cost (e.g. `Wungle's Great Sucking (35)`). The tag is
  gated to a column boundary — the name must sit at line start or after 2+
  spaces *and* be followed by 2+ spaces or line end — so it only fires in
  the columnar listing. Ordinary prose ("You prepare to cast … on
  yourself.") and chat mentions stay untagged (verified against real game
  logs). Spell names keep their usual by-tier colour everywhere.
- **Total summary.** After the listing settles, a colour-coded line —
  `Total spell size: 337 / 415  (78 free)` — reports how much of your
  mindspace you're using (green under budget, yellow at exactly full,
  red over).
- **`/mindspace`** (alias `/mind`) prints an on-demand breakdown: your
  available capacity, used size, and every known spell sorted
  largest-first so the mindspace hogs are obvious.

The known-spell set is seeded from the `spells` listing and kept live by
`remember` / `forget` lines, then persisted per character — so
`/mindspace` stays accurate between listings and across relogs. Running
`spells <category>` re-scopes only that category, leaving the others
intact.

The available-mindspace total comes from
[discworld-vitals](https://github.com/wizardquack/mallardx-discworld-vitals)'
skill snapshot (run its `/skills-refresh` once). Without it, sizes and the
used total still work — only the capacity figure is withheld, with a nudge
to refresh.

On every change the plugin emits `net.mallard.discworld.mindspace.updated`
`{ charname, total, used, free, known_count }` (`total`/`free` are `nil`
until a skill snapshot lands) so other plugins can surface the budget.

> Not to be confused with Major Shield (divine "ms" protection), which
> this plugin also tracks separately.

## Cross-plugin events in depth

This plugin emits `net.mallard.discworld.shield.up` and
`net.mallard.discworld.shield.down` for both self and other-player
shield state changes. Payload shape:

```
subject  = "self" | "<PlayerName>"
type     = "tpa" | "eff" | "ccc" | "bug" | "ms"
# optional, populated by type:
percent, glow, previous_glow, previous_percent  -- tpa
item                                            -- eff
hits, duration_seconds                          -- tpa (and eff for self)
silent                                          -- eff (intentional drops)
```

v1 implements TPA and EFF for both subjects. CCC/BUG/MS are reserved in
the event grammar and will be added in a follow-up plan.

Consumers today:
- `discworld-vitals` — self-only; filters by `subject == "self"` and
  drives the EFF indicator + TPA stat cells.
- `discworld-grouping` — self + other; drives the five-pill shield row
  per group member.

## Credit

Many thanks to Quow and Oki, whose work on similar plugins was
invaluable in designing and building this one. `/spellskill`'s TM
ordering follows tt_dw's `/spell_tm_list`.

plugins.latest_readme:
# Mallard Discworld MDT

A [Mallard](https://mallard.vnsf.xyz) plugin for [Discworld MUD](https://discworld.starturtle.net/lpc/) that turns the `room.writtenmap` GMCP frame into a scored "Nearby" panel.

## What it does

Each time you move, Discworld sends a GMCP `room.writtenmap` payload listing who and what is visible in adjacent rooms (the same data you'd see by typing `map door text`). This plugin parses it and renders a sortable, scored panel:

```
  N   [5]  Sgt Detritus, 2 watchmen
  NE  [3]  3 bystanders, beggar
  2E  [2]  Carrot
  S   [1]  cat, 2 ravens
```

Rooms are sorted by score; the panel hides rooms below a threshold (configurable).

## Radar panel

A second panel, **Radar**, shows the same rooms as a 5x5 map of the ground
around you, with your own square in the middle:

```
  .    .    .    .    .
  .   2wm  .    .    .
  .    .    @   3bg  .
  .    .   6pg  .    .
  .    .    .    .    .
```

Each room's direction is summed into a square — "one north and one east" and
"one northeast" land on the same cell and merge. Hovering a square shows its
full contents; the squares themselves show as much as the panel allows, so
resizing the panel shows more.

Backgrounds shade by the square's own score, on fixed bands (1, 2-3, 4-6,
7-10, 11+) running deep blue through violet and magenta to burnt orange, so
the same room always looks the same colour as you move. The busiest square in
view is outlined. The count in the corner ramps green through red, and the
eight rooms one step away sit on a lighter ground than the ring beyond them.

Rooms with no compass square — up, down, shipboard directions (fore/aft/port/
starboard), and anything more than two rooms out — are listed underneath the
grid in the usual scored rows rather than being dropped.

Both panels are driven by the same pushes, so you can dock either one, or
both at once, and place them wherever your layout wants them.

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `mdt` | Show command list |
| `mdt help` | Show command list |
| `mdt list [pattern]` | Show match list, optionally filtered |
| `mdt add <pattern> [score] [colour]` | Add a match |
| `mdt remove <pattern>\|<n>` | Remove by pattern text or 1-based index |
| `mdt clear` | Wipe match list (this character only) |

Patterns are case-insensitive substrings by default. Wrap a pattern in `/.../` for Lua-pattern matching:

```
mdt add watchman 3 red
mdt add /^(sgt|cpt) %a+/ 5 yellow
```

Colours: `red`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `blue`, `magenta`, `white`, `grey`, plus `bold-` variants.

## Settings

- **Default score per entity** — applied to entities matching no entry (default: 1).
- **Hide rooms scoring below** — threshold for omitting rooms from the panel (default: 0).
- **Max rooms shown in panel** — caps the visible rows (default: 20).
- **Shorten and group names in Radar** — collapse each square's contents into
  counted groups keyed on the last word of each name, so "angry hoplite" and
  "sassy hoplite" read as `2xhoplite`. Words shorten to three letters only in
  squares too small to hold them, so a wide panel stays readable. Off by
  default; the full list is always on the square's tooltip.
- **Radar panel shading** — shade squares by score, use one colour for every
  occupied room, or no background colour at all.
- **Radar colour — score 1 / 2-3 / 4-6 / 7-10 / 11+** — one hex colour per
  band. Left blank, a band follows the current theme: each is a hue off the
  flame ramp (cold blue → hot orange) tinted into the theme's own background,
  so it comes through as a saturated dark on a dark theme, a pale tint on a
  light one, and picks up the background's cast on a tinted theme. A value
  overrides that band in every theme; anything that isn't a hex colour is
  treated as blank.
  The score 1 colour doubles as the fill for the "one colour for every occupied
  room" mode — that mode means "something is here, never mind how much", which
  is what the bottom band already says.

## Storage

Match lists are stored per-character, keyed by `char.info.name`.

## Development

```sh
luarocks install busted  # one-time
busted                    # run unit tests
```

Spec lives at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-mdt-v0.1-design.md`
(gitignored — keep your local copy in sync with intent).

## Credit

Many thanks to Quow and Oki, whose work on similar plugins was
invaluable in designing and building this one.

# Discworld Mission Manager

A [Mallard](https://github.com/wizardquack/mallard) plugin that tracks Discworld's
repeatable jobs and missions — **cooldowns**, **per-mission XP**, and an **XP-per-hour
ranking** so you always know the best thing to do next.

## v1 coverage

| Family | Missions | Cooldown |
|--------|----------|----------|
| AM Job Market (Mr Werks) | 13 employment writs (Thirst Quencher → Expert Street Maintenance Technician) | 1h from completion |
| Dead Letter Office (Frank) | 9 letters DLA–DLI | 1h from completion |
| Sam Slager | sausage delivery (single mission) | 1h from completion |

XP is **observed + seeded**: never-done missions show a seeded estimate; once you
complete a mission the real awarded XP (read from "You have been awarded N experience
points…") is used thereafter.

## Panel

Dock the **Missions** panel (right side by default). It shows your active missions
(several can run at once — the game allows one active job per family, e.g. a Werks job
alongside a dead letter delivery) and an
**On cooldown** list with live countdowns. The **Ready** list (missions available now,
ranked by XP/hour) is off by default — turn on *Show ready missions in panel* to enable it.
Right-click for "Reset all cooldowns".

## Commands

All commands are also available under the shorter alias `/mm` (e.g. `/mm list`).

| Command | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `/missions` or `/missions help` | Show command help |
| `/missions list` | Full ranked table of every mission (active runtimes + ready XP/rate + cooldown countdowns). Always shows everything, regardless of the panel display settings. |
| `/missions status` | Your active missions and how long each has been running |
| `/missions cancel [job]` | Clear a stuck "active" mission (e.g. after a completion the plugin missed). With several missions active, name the one to clear — bare `cancel` lists them. |
| `/missions reset <job>` | Clear one mission's cooldown (e.g. `/mm reset gofer`) |

`<job>` is any case-insensitive fragment of the label shown in `/missions list` (or an
exact internal key — the disambiguation output prints those). `/mm cancel lackey`,
`/mm reset dlc`, and `/mm reset far away` all resolve (no quotes needed — the fragment
may contain spaces); an ambiguous fragment lists the candidates instead of guessing.
| `/missions reset` | Clear ALL cooldowns (run twice within 10s to confirm) |

## Settings

- **Travel time estimate (s)** — added to each mission's measured time in the rate math (default 120).
- **Desktop notification when ready** — OS notification on expiry (default off; a note always prints).
- **Ready-alert XP/hr floor** — only alert for missions at/above this rate (default 0).
- **Show ready missions in panel** — show the panel's Ready section at all (default **off**). Does not affect `/missions list`.
- **Show never-done missions in panel** — when the Ready section is shown, also include missions you've never completed, using their seeded XP (default on). Does not affect `/missions list`.

## Known v1 limitations

- Sausages are a single mission; plain/spiced and per-critter splits are deferred.
- A late-delivered difficult letter (no award line) isn't recorded that round.
- If the plugin loads while a mission is already active, that completion may be missed
  (start is latched from your outgoing `apply`/`offer` command).
- No mapper integration — travel time is a flat setting.

## Development

Pure-logic modules (`engine`, `xp`, `cooldowns`, `store`, `format`, `commands`, families)
are unit-tested with the system `lua`:

```sh
for f in tests/*_test.lua; do echo "== $f =="; lua "$f" || exit 1; done
```

# Discworld Sailing

A Discworld sailing-mission plugin with three pieces:

1. **Highlights** — ~90 regex highlights for sea serpents, kraken,
   fires, ice, helming, rope/hull condition strings, dragon
   wrangling, and sun-sighting position reports.
2. **Smuggling stat panel** — Tracks mission cooldown, per-leg
   timers + XP, monster fight time + XP, and the running voyage total
   in a panel.
3. **TTS mode** — an optional set of spoken callouts for notable sailing
   events (off by default; one setting to toggle).

## TTS mode

Turn on **Speak notable sailing events (TTS)** in the plugin's settings to
have Mallard read out a curated set of callouts through its text-to-speech.
The toggle takes effect immediately (no reload). Voice, rate and volume are
configured globally under **Settings → Speech**.

What it speaks, all on a dedicated `sailing` speech channel so callouts queue
in order:

- **Milestones** — "Voyage begun", each weather stage as it arrives
  (Fog / Hail / Gale / Storm / Calm seas), "Leg _n_ complete",
  monster defeated, and "Voyage complete" / "Voyage failed".
- **Urgent cues** — a monster spawn ("Kraken!" / "Serpent!") and a serpent
  strike ("Run!") *interrupt* whatever is queued and speak immediately.
- **Line cues** — "Ship under way", fire started, and boiler run dry.
  Each is debounced so a repeating line can't say itself twice, and they
  stay silent outside a live voyage.

The milestone callouts are driven by the same mission state machine that
feeds the stat panel, so the spoken set stays in lock-step with the panel's
tracking rather than matching lines independently.

### Sail warning

A separate setting, **Speak a sail warning before the cooldown ends (TTS)**
(off by default), speaks once when the smuggling cooldown gets down to a set
time. It works whether or not TTS mode is on. Two more settings control it:

- **Sail warning — minutes left**: when to speak it (default 10).
- **Sail warning — text to speak**: what to say (default "10 minute sail
  warning"). If you change the minutes, update the text to match.

If you log in or `su` with up to a minute less than that left, it still
speaks. Any later and it stays quiet.

## Stat panel

A 1-second timer drives every cell:

- **Cooldown** — counts down 2h after each mission starts; persisted across
  restarts via `storage`.
- **Stage** — current weather stage name while sailing.
- **Leg 1..4 / Monster** — `<name> mm:ss (xp)` per stage; XP fills in when
  the leg-finished message fires.
- **Voyage** — total elapsed time + summed XP across all legs.

The cooldown and the last-voyage rows are stored per character, keyed by
`char.info.name` — the in-game cooldown is per-character, so a world with
several of your characters tracks each one separately. The panel re-reads
the current character's data on login and on `su` (but not mid-voyage).
Before the character name is known, a `_default` bucket is used.

### Voyage keymap

The plugin ships a built-in **sailing-numpad** keymap layer (8-direction numpad
steering: numpad8/2/4/6 → fore/aft/port/starboard, corners for diagonals).
It appears in Settings → Keymaps and can be edited freely — rebind the keys or
change the commands to taste; your edits persist.

The layer is activated at voyage start and deactivated at voyage end
automatically. This is controlled by the **Use sailing-numpad keymap during
voyages** setting (on by default); turn it off to leave your keymap untouched
during voyages.

### Debug aliases

| alias            | effect                                              |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `!startMission`  | Force-start the mission state machine.              |
| `!endMission`    | Force-end (use if a stage trigger missed and the panel is stuck). |
| `!nextStage <X>` | Force a transition to weather stage `X`.            |
| `!sailData`      | Dump the current trip stages + XP table via `mud.note`. |

## Credit

Thank you to Kiki for the wonderful Smuggler's toolbox plugin, which helped immensely in sorting through the regex this plugin's panel.

# Discworld Vitals

Vitals panel for Discworld MUD, with:

- HP / GP / burden bars
- XP, XP/hr, and XP/hr over time chart
- realtime shielding indicators (EFF / CCC / BUG / MS / TPA)

Additionally this plugin provides skill-, stat-, and xp-aware goal
tracking for your characters. Enter /goals to get started, or /skill
<skill> to inspect a single skill's level, bonus, and the stats that
feed it — add an optional number (e.g. /skill ma.sp.of 550) to see what
level a target bonus needs and what bonus a target level gives, with a
one-click "add goal" for either.

It also keeps a history of your skill increases — TMs, advances, and
teaching alike. Whenever you type `hskills` in game, every line it prints
is recorded with its exact time. Increases `hskills` never showed (a
session that ended before you typed it) are inferred from what changed
between /skills-refresh runs and dated as a range ("Oct 2–4"). Browse it
with /skill-history (or /sh; last week, every skill), /skill-history all,
/skill-history <skill>, or a whole branch like /skill-history fi.ra,
with windows like 3d, 2w, 6m, today or all; /skill also lists a skill's ten most recent increases. Run
/skill-history backpopulate once to import every `hskills` you've typed
before from this world's Mallard logs. Each increase is filed under the
character who was logged in at the time (from the GMCP char.info Mallard
logged with it), so one run fills in every character that has played through
the world. It needs Mallard's plugin log search and the "Search this world's
log history" permission; running it again only adds what's missing.

It also tracks how much xp each character earns per day. /xp shows the
last week, one row a day: xp earned, the xp value of the day's TMs, the
total of those two, time online, xp per hour online, and xp spent
(Discworld's xp is unspent xp, so advancing at your guild is counted
separately rather than wiping out the day's earnings), with a total row and
your best day. A TM is valued at what the same level would have cost from
an optimal teacher; TMs are told apart from paid advances in your skill
history by whether an xp drop of the right size paid for them. The total is
what xp/hr and your best day are based on. Language
skills sit outside the xp system, so their levels aren't counted as TMs. Try /xp today (hour by hour), /xp 2w, /xp 6m or /xp all, and
/xp <character> for an alt. The XP card on the panel shows today's
total so far; click it for the breakdown. Run /xp backpopulate
once to rebuild earlier days from this world's Mallard logs — it replays
the GMCP char.vitals readings Mallard logged, for every character that's
played through the world, and only fills hours that aren't already
recorded. Run it again after updating, even if you already have: it also
picks up past xp drops, which the TMs column needs to spot paid advances.

To share how it's going, /xp say tells the room what you've earned in the
last hour (e.g. "412k xp in the last hour."), and /xp gsay says it on the
group channel. Add session or today for xp since you connected or since
midnight, with time online and xp/hr: "1.24M xp this session (2h 14m, 553k
xp/hr)." Add total to include the value of your TMs, as in the /xp total
column: /xp say today total says "3.36M xp incl. TMs today (5h 40m, 593k
xp/hr)." The same options are under Say XP and Group say XP when you
right-click the panel.

## A note on cross-plugin events

This plugin has an optional dependency on
[discworld-magic](https://github.com/wizardquack/mallardx-discworld-magic)
for receiving shielding event data. If you don't have it, no harm
done, but if you, Vitals will automatically subscribe to realtime
shielding events from the Magic plugin.

Vitals also **emits** `net.mallard.discworld.gp.full` (payload
`{ subject = "self", gp, maxgp }`) the moment your GP refills to
maximum, so peer plugins can react — e.g. resume casting. It fires once
on each refill to full (edge-triggered on the not-full → full
transition), the complement of the inbound
`net.mallard.discworld.gp.zero` event Vitals subscribes to.

## Credit

Many thanks to Quow and Oki, whose work on similar plugins was
invaluable in designing and building this one.
